editorial.headline: Visual Art Creation, and Bali’s PMA Stop
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this visual-art activity is nevertheless blocked from PMA registration across Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity concerns the creation and production of visual artworks through varied media and methods, whether the resulting work is tangible or intangible. Its natural inhabitants are independent makers: sculptors, painters, cartoonists, calligraphers, carvers, sketch artists and craft artists. It also expressly reaches digital visual art and artworks made with light installations. A studio practice, a solo artist’s output or a production-led art business can all fit the description when the central act is making the visual work. The unifying fact is not the medium but authorship and production of the artwork itself.

The boundary is deliberately narrow. The record keeps this category with original visual-art creation rather than the broader orbit of creative, presentation, commercial, technical, conservation or event activity that may surround a work of art. That distinction matters for registration. A business does not enter this activity merely because it works near the arts; its activity must be the creation and production of the artwork. In that sense the code gives independent artists and art-making enterprises a common, precise home, without stretching the definition into a catch-all label for culture.

All four stated business scales—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—are open to it. Nationally, its PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign investor, that is an unequivocal national position: full foreign ownership is permitted within this activity’s national classification. It is an important starting point for an art practice or company, but it is not the end of the location analysis. The Bali position must be read separately, on its own stated terms.

Bali changes the result decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, the record assigns every scope an OSS risk of Low or Medium-Low; those risk levels place it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration. The Bali record marks the activity as blocked by risk class and attributes the block to the moratorium in force since May 2026. National openness has not disappeared, but it does not overrule the Bali restriction: in Bali, the 100% national ceiling cannot be used to secure a PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not overrule Bali’s permanent bar on PMA registration for this activity.
